title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (November 2026 data) — the first annual-revision edition of 2027, 4:00 p.m. ET, the Tuesday after MLK
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes). The 2027 table's January row reads '19' in the Monthly column with the Quarterly, gross-external-debt and Annual columns all EMPTY — a single-cut release, unlike the double 2026-12-15 — under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month November 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-09 on the bar the four TIC siblings and mts-october-2026-11-12 set — one named Treasury primary plus independent mechanical corroboration — with the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching, not the tic-monthly-2026-11-18 sweep that discovered it. The corroboration, recomputed from scratch and unusually strong here: the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule, with the 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holidays excluded, puts January 2027's 11th business day on 2027-01-19 EXACTLY (offset +0 business days). January 2027 carries TWO federal holidays (New Year's Day 01-01, MLK 01-18), so a holiday-BLIND reading of the same rule would land on 2027-01-15 — four days earlier. Treasury published 01-19. This date is therefore the single cleanest discriminator on the published 2026-27 schedule between the holiday-aware and holiday-blind conventions, and it sides with holiday-aware, which is the convention every sibling ledger in this series has assumed. Across all 24 published 2026-27 dates that convention lands in-window 22 times and hits 9 exactly; both misses (2026-01-15, 2026-07-14) publish EARLIER than the rule's floor, so a date sitting inside the window is never one of the failure modes. TSY: is extended from auction schedule to release schedule on the precedent mts-august-2026-09-11, mts-october-2026-11-12 and tic-monthly-2026-09-16/10-16/11-18/12-15 already recorded. CONFIRMED COVERS THE SCHEDULED DATE AND NOTHING ELSE: the same page carries the standing notice 'When Federal Government offices in Washington D.C. are closed on a release date, that date will be revised after offices reopen'. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-monthly-2026-11-18`, now shadowed. WHAT THIS EDITION IS FOR, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: it is a Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct release, which Treasury's own note (c) says 'reflect[s] revised data for the past year' against 'the prior 3 months' for every other release. This session measured that claim for the first time in this series, by diffing 29 archived press-notice PDF vintages (2024-01 through 2026-08) cell by cell. Revision editions really do restate more: mean absolute revision to an overlapping monthly cell is $5.01bn at a Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct vintage against $1.67bn at an ordinary one (t=+3.93, n=6 vs 10) once the February/March vintages are set aside as a DIFFERENT and larger mechanism -- the annual-survey benchmark feed plus footnote 9's series break, which moved a closed calendar-year total by up to $745.9bn. With Feb/Mar left in, the same test is a flat null (p=0.78), and both readings are on the record in the ledger. Scale keeps it honest: $5bn sits against a median monthly value of $102.8bn on the lines it moves, so a revision edition nudges the observations a forward test is scored against by roughly 5 percent -- real, quantified, and not enough to flip a sign. This SHARPENS the premise the proposal filed under, which asserted the revision 'can move the very observations those tests were scored against' without a number. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). THE CORRIDOR IS THIN, which is this date's other distinguishing fact: 8 tracked events within +/-5 days against 27 for 2026-12-15, no CPI/PPI/retail-sales cluster tracked in the window, and a scored session (2027-01-20) carrying only vix-expiration-2027-01-20. That makes this the second cleanly testable TIC release on the calendar after 2026-10-16. It also sits inside the fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16 window ahead of fomc-2027-01-27, and is the destination slot FT-tic-monthly-2026-12-15-2 names if a funding lapse merges the December release forward.
